family: volatility gates (overnight-range, prior-day-range, ATR regime filters on London trend pullback)

variants.name: BASE (no gate)
variants.note: sanity check: reproduces reference numbers exactly

variants.name: a_ONrange>=med20 (00:00->trigger vs trailing 20d same-time median)
variants.note: trims 2024 by 43% but destroys 79% of test profit; per-trade netR falls

variants.name: b_ONrange>=1.25x_med20
variants.note: tighter threshold pushes test expectancy negative — high-vol subset is the WORSE subset

variants.name: c_prevFullDayRange>=med20 (partial days <800min excluded)
variants.note: best single gate: keeps 57% of test $, trims 2024 loss 39%, cuts maxDD 29%

variants.name: d_ATR14_M15>=med200bar
variants.note: best per-trade quality among singles but flips 2023 negative and drops test $ 69%

variants.name: e_combo c AND d
variants.note: biggest 2024 fix (-67% of loss) and halves maxDD, but only 33 test trades (LOW-N) and 74% of test $ gone

insight: Volatility gates do NOT fix 2024: every gate leaves 2024 solidly negative while cutting test netR below the base's +0.425, meaning the 2024 losers were spread across volatility regimes rather than concentrated in quiet tape — in fact the high-vol subsets have worse per-trade expectancy (variant b goes negative). The gates reduce dollars roughly proportionally to trade count, so they act as blunt position-throttles (lower maxDD ~$40k->$20-29k) rather than edge filters. Prior-full-day-range >= 20d median (c) is the least-bad tradeoff, but the family should be deprioritized as the 2024 fix — look at direction/regime (e.g. short-side or trend-quality) families instead.

variants.name: tgt_1.5R
variants.note: Highest WR but worst test E[R]; shrinks 2024 loss ~1/3 by capping winners

variants.name: tgt_2R
variants.note: Best PF and best risk-adjusted: 2024 loss -33%, maxDD -30%, keeps 81% of base test net

variants.name: tgt_2.5R
variants.note: Middle ground, dominated by 2R on PF/DD and by 3R on net

variants.name: tgt_3R_BASE
variants.note: UNCHANGED BASE, reproduces reference numbers exactly

variants.name: tgt_4R
variants.note: Strictly worse than base: lower E[R], same 2024 disaster, worst maxDD

variants.name: tgt_2R_BE@1R
variants.note: BE-at-+1R (applied next bar) converts many winners to scratches; smallest 2024 loss and lowest maxDD but big E[R] cost

variants.name: part50@1.5R_run3R_BE
variants.note: Fractional 50% exit at 1.5R + BE runner, single $5 RT commission; smoother than base but dominated by plain 2R

insight: Target geometry cannot FIX 2024 — every variant still loses $18-28k there because the damage is losing trades (bad entries in chop), not winner management; exits only scale the bleed. Within that limit, 2R target is the clear risk-adjusted winner: it cuts the 2024 loss by a third and maxDD by 30% ($40k to $28k) while keeping the best test PF (1.75) and 81% of base test net, and BE/partial mechanics only subtract further (BE-at-1R scratches too many eventual winners). The base's 3R edge on raw net_test comes almost entirely from 2026 trend runs, i.e. it buys extra tail upside at the price of the deepest drawdown — the 2024 fix must come from an entry/regime gate, not the bracket.

variants.name: M15 (base)
variants.note: Sanity check passed: exactly reproduces reference (netE[R] +0.425, WR 42%, PF 1.71, +$55,975 test, 2024 -$28,320, maxDD ~$40k).

variants.name: M5
variants.note: 3.3x test sample and it is decisively negative: loses in test AND in 2024. Softens 2024 only by trading smaller noise-stops, while flipping 2025-26 from +$56k to -$30k. Kills, not confirms.

variants.name: M30
variants.note: Only 75 trades full-span (LOW-N): the London window holds ~9 M30 bars so setups barely occur; essentially flat everywhere. Uninformative, not a fix.

insight: M5's 3.3x larger test sample KILLS rather than confirms the London edge (netR -0.153, PF 0.80, -$30,420 test with WR collapsing to 24%), meaning the M15 result does not generalize across resample and is likely a timeframe-specific artifact rather than a robust pullback effect. Neither alternative fixes 2024 usefully: M5 shrinks the 2024 loss only by shrinking everything (and destroys 2025-26), and M30 has too few trades (n=75 full-span) to trade or to learn from. Timeframe is not the lever for the 2024 problem; the base M15 stays best within this family but its edge should be treated with heightened overfit suspicion.

variants.name: base_0300-0745_flat0925
variants.note: Sanity check: reproduces stated base numbers exactly.

variants.name: early_0300-0500_flat0925
variants.note: Early window is the weak third: 2025 goes negative; low-N test.

variants.name: late_0500-0745_flat0925
variants.note: Late window carries ~82% of test net with 69% of trades; 2024 still -$20k.

variants.name: base_fills_flat0745
variants.note: No NY-open exposure: 2024 loss halved, maxDD halved to $19.6k, test net still +$40k, PF improves.

variants.name: base_fills_flat1200
variants.note: Holding through NY open amplifies everything: best test net but worst 2024 and worst maxDD.

insight: The edge lives in the late 05:00-07:45 window (netR +0.53 vs +0.20 early), but no fill sub-window fixes 2024 — all timing slices lose there. NY-open exposure is a leverage dial, not an edge source: flattening at 07:45 halves both the 2024 loss (-$14.2k) and full-span maxDD ($19.6k) while keeping +$40k test with PF 1.75, whereas holding to 12:00 maximizes test net (+$77.6k) but deepens 2024 to -$33k and maxDD to $45k. Best risk-adjusted fix is flatten-at-07:45; the 2024 problem itself is not a session-timing artifact.

variants.name: BASE wick vol<1.0 mkt
variants.note: reproduces reference exactly

variants.name: touch-reclaim vol<1.0 mkt
variants.note: prior close beyond 50MA then reclaim; halves 2024 loss but also halves test $

variants.name: wick vol-none mkt
variants.note: vol filter removed: biggest test $, but 2024 still bad and DD worst

variants.name: wick vol<0.8 mkt
variants.note: tighter fade helps per-trade R, only partially fixes 2024

variants.name: wick vol<1.2 mkt
variants.note: looser fade ~ base; no 2024 fix

variants.name: wick vol<1.0 +close>20MA mkt
variants.note: deeper-trend gate: excellent per-trade stats but LOW-N (36 test)

variants.name: wick vol<1.0 limit@50MA
variants.note: limit at 50MA next bar (~61% fill): 2024 loss -57%, keeps 75% of test $, DD halved

variants.name: touch vol<1.0 limit@50MA
variants.note: 2024 nearly flat, netR +1.0R, lowest DD; LOW-N (40 test)

variants.name: wick vol<0.8 +close>20MA mkt
variants.note: over-filtered: n=14 test, not tradeable evidence

variants.name: touch vol-none mkt
variants.note: touch trigger alone (no vol filter) fixes 2024 with decent n and $

insight: The 2024 bleed comes from the wick trigger itself, not the volume filter: requiring the prior bar to actually CLOSE beyond the 50MA and then reclaim (touch-reclaim) cuts 2024 from -$28.3k to -$3.9k while keeping ~68% of test profit at n=108, and it does so best with the vol filter removed entirely (vol fade is roughly noise across thresholds). The limit-at-50MA entry independently adds ~+0.15R per trade and halves drawdown by buying the retest instead of chasing next open, and stacking it on touch (touch+limit) nearly zeroes 2024 with +1.0R/trade and $10.9k full-span maxDD, though at n=40 it needs more sample before trusting.

family: robustness dissection of BASE (long/short split, mirror counter-baseline, ex-2024)

variants.name: base
variants.note: 2024 quarterly net: Q1 -$7,270 (n=32), Q2 -$6,955 (n=31), Q3 -$8,940 (n=29), Q4 -$5,155 (n=18) - every quarter negative; 49 of 60 trading days negative; 5 worst days only -$8,165 of the -$28,320

variants.name: base_long_only
variants.note: 2024: 77 trades, WR 16.9%, mean -0.434R; test edge intact but 2026 mostly short-driven

variants.name: base_short_only
variants.note: 2024: 33 trades, WR 9.1%, mean -0.723R - worst per-trade; carries most of 2026 test $

variants.name: mirror_counter
variants.note: same triggers fading direction, stop=swing extreme; negative every year EXCEPT 2024 where it made +$11,295 (+0.083R over 102 trades)

variants.name: base_ex2024
variants.note: context only: removing 2024 cuts full-span maxDD from $40,195 to $11,875 - the drawdown IS the 2024 bleed

insight: 2024's failure is in BOTH directions (longs -$16.6k over 77 trades, shorts -$11.7k over just 33 with a brutal 9% WR / -0.72R per trade) and is a steady all-year bleed, not a few disasters: every quarter negative, 49 of 60 trade-days negative, and the 5 worst days explain only $8.2k of the $28.3k. Critically, the mirror counter-baseline is POSITIVE in 2024 (+$11.3k) while negative in 2023/2025/2026, meaning 2024 was trend-INVERTED for this setup - London 50MA pullbacks kept going through the MA rather than chopping both ways - so a filter must detect regime (pullback follow-through failing), not just cut trade count. The full-span $40k maxDD is essentially the 2024 bleed itself (ex-2024 maxDD is only $11.9k).
